children.text: || namo ratnatrayāya ||
children.translated_text: Homage to the <s>Ratnatraya</s> (Three Jewels)!

children.text: sarvadoṣavinirmuktaṃ guṇaiḥ sarvair alaṃkṛtaṃ |
children.translated_text: Free from all faults, adorned with all virtues —

children.text: praṇamya sarvajñam ahaṃ sarvasattvaikabāndhavaṃ || RATNA_01.01
children.translated_text: having bowed to the Omniscient One, the sole kinsman of all beings, // RATNA 1.1

children.text: dharmam ekāntakalyāṇaṃ rāja [ n dha ] rmodayāya te |
children.translated_text: I shall speak the <s>Dharma</s> (teaching), which is exclusively auspicious, for the arising of your royal <s>Dharma</s>,

children.text: vakṣyāmi dharmaḥ siddhiṃ hi yāti saddharmabhājane || RATNA_01.02
children.translated_text: for the <s>Dharma</s> succeeds when [it finds] a worthy vessel of the true teaching. // RATNA 1.2

children.text: prāg dharmābhyudayo yatra paścān naiḥśreyasodayaḥ |
children.translated_text: Where first [there is] the arising of worldly prosperity (<s>abhyudaya</s>), and afterward the arising of the highest good (<s>naiḥśreyasa</s>) —

children.text: samprāpyābhyudayaṃ yasmād eti naiḥśreyasaṃ kramāt || RATNA_01.03
children.translated_text: since, having attained worldly prosperity, one proceeds gradually to the highest good. // RATNA 1.3

children.text: sukham abhyudaya [ s tatra mokṣo ] naiḥśreyaso mataḥ |
children.translated_text: Happiness is worldly prosperity; liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>) is considered the highest good.

children.text: asya sādhanasaṃkṣepaḥ śraddhāprajñe samāsataḥ || RATNA_01.04
children.translated_text: The summary of the means to these two is, in brief, faith (<s>śraddhā</s>) and wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>). // RATNA 1.4

children.text: śrāddhatvād bhajate dharmaṃ prājñatvād vetti tattvataḥ |
children.translated_text: Through faith one follows the <s>Dharma</s>; through wisdom one knows [it] as it truly is.

children.text: prajñā pradhānaṃ tv anayoḥ śraddhā pūrvaṅgamāsya tu || RATNA_01.05
children.translated_text: Of these two, wisdom is the principal; but faith is its prerequisite. // RATNA 1.5

children.text: chandād dveṣād bhayān mohād yo dharmaṃ nātivartate |
children.translated_text: One who does not transgress the <s>Dharma</s> out of desire, hatred, fear, or delusion —

children.text: sa śrāddha iti vijñeyaḥ śreyaso bhājanaṃ param || RATNA_01.06
children.translated_text: that one should be known as a person of faith, a supreme vessel for the good. // RATNA 1.6

children.text: kāyavāṅmānasaṃ karma sarvaṃ samyak parīkṣya yaḥ |
children.translated_text: One who, having thoroughly examined all actions of body, speech, and mind,

children.text: parātmahitam ājñāya sadā kuryāt sa paṇḍitaḥ || RATNA_01.07
children.translated_text: knowing what benefits both self and others, always acts accordingly — that one is wise. // RATNA 1.7

children.text: ahiṃsā cauryaviratiḥ paradāravivarjanam |
children.translated_text: Non-violence, abstaining from theft, avoiding another's spouse,

children.text: mithyāpaiśunyapāruṣyābaddhavādeṣu saṃyamaḥ || RATNA_01.08
children.translated_text: restraint from falsehood, slander, harsh speech, and idle talk, // RATNA 1.8

children.text: lobhavyāpādanāstik [ yadṛṣṭīnāṃ parivarjanaṃ |
children.translated_text: abandoning covetousness, malice, and nihilistic views —

children.text: ete karmapathā ] śuklā daśa kṛṣṇā viparyayāt || RATNA_01.09
children.translated_text: these are the ten white paths of action; the black ones are their opposites. // RATNA 1.9

children.text: amadyapānaṃ svājīvo 'vihiṃsā dānam ādarāt |
children.translated_text: Abstaining from intoxicants, a pure livelihood, non-harming, giving with respect,

children.text: pūjyapūjā ca maitrī ca dharmaś caiṣa samāsataḥ || RATNA_01.10
children.translated_text: honoring the worthy, and loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>) — this too is the <s>Dharma</s> in brief. // RATNA 1.10

children.text: śarīratāpanād dharmaḥ kevalān [ nāsti tena hi ] |
children.translated_text: The <s>Dharma</s> does not consist solely in mortification of the body, for thereby

children.text: [ 2,a ] na paradrohaviratir na pareṣām anugrahaḥ || RATNA_01.11
children.translated_text: there is neither cessation of harm to others nor benefit to others. // RATNA 1.11

children.text: dānaśīlakṣamāspaṣṭaṃ yaḥ saddharmamahāpatham |
children.translated_text: One who, disregarding the great highway of the true <s>Dharma</s>, made clear by generosity (<s>dāna</s>), moral conduct (<s>śīla</s>), and forbearance (<s>kṣamā</s>),

children.text: anādṛtya vrajet kāyakleśago daṇḍakotpathaiḥ || RATNA_01.12
children.translated_text: would go by the byways of bodily austerity through punitive practices — // RATNA 1.12

children.text: sa saṃsārāṭavīṃ ghorām anantajanapādapām |
children.translated_text: that one enters the dreadful wilderness of <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence), with its countless trees of [successive] births,

children.text: kleśavyālāvalīḍhāṅgaḥ sudīrghaṃ pratipadyate || RATNA_01.13
children.translated_text: limbs licked by the serpents of the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), for a very long time. // RATNA 1.13

children.text: hiṃsayā jāyate 'lpāyuḥ bahvābādho vihiṃsayā |
children.translated_text: From violence one is born with a short life; from harming others, with much affliction;

children.text: cauryeṇa bhogavyasanī saśa [ truḥ ] paradārikaḥ || RATNA_01.14
children.translated_text: from theft, loss of possessions; from adultery, [one gains] enemies. // RATNA 1.14

children.text: pratyākhyānaṃ mṛṣāvādāt paiśunyāt mitrabhedanam |
children.translated_text: From falsehood, rejection [by others]; from slander, the breaking of friendships;

children.text: apriyaśravaṇaṃ raukṣyād abāddhād durbhagaṃ vacaḥ || RATNA_01.15
children.translated_text: from harsh speech, hearing what is unpleasant; from idle talk, undignified speech. // RATNA 1.15

children.text: manorathān hanty abhidhyā vyāpādo bhayadaḥ smṛtaḥ |
children.translated_text: Covetousness destroys [one's] aspirations; malice is said to bring fear;

children.text: mithyādṛṣṭiḥ kudṛṣṭitvaṃ madyapānaṃ matibhramaḥ || RATNA_01.16
children.translated_text: wrong views lead to false beliefs; drinking intoxicants leads to mental confusion. // RATNA 1.16

children.text: apradānena dāridryaṃ mithyājivena vañcanā |
children.translated_text: From not giving, poverty; from wrong livelihood, deception;

children.text: stambhena duḥkuḷīnatvam alpaujaskatvam īrṣayā || RATNA_01.17
children.translated_text: from arrogance, low birth; from envy, lack of splendor. // RATNA 1.17

children.text: krodhād durvarṇatā maurkhyam apraśnena vipaścitām |
children.translated_text: From anger, ugly appearance; from stupidity [in] not questioning the wise —

children.text: phalam etan manuṣyatve sarvebhyaḥ prāk ca durgatiḥ || RATNA_01.18
children.translated_text: this is the fruit in the human realm, and before all [of these], a bad rebirth (<s>durgati</s>). // RATNA 1.18

children.text: esāṃ akuśalākhyānāṃ vipāko yaḥ prakīrtitaḥ |
children.translated_text: The ripening that has been proclaimed for these actions called unwholesome —

children.text: kuśalānāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ viparītaḥ phalodayaḥ || RATNA_01.19
children.translated_text: for all the wholesome ones, the arising of fruit is the opposite. // RATNA 1.19

children.text: lobho dveṣaś ca mohas ca tajjaṃ karmeti cāśubham |
children.translated_text: Greed, hatred, and delusion, and action born from them — this is unwholesome;

children.text: alobhāmohādveṣāś ca tajjaṃ karmetarac chubhaṃ || RATNA_01.20
children.translated_text: non-greed, non-delusion, non-hatred, and action born from them — this other is wholesome. // RATNA 1.20

children.text: aśubhāt sarvaduḥkhāni sarvadurgatayas tathā |
children.translated_text: From the unwholesome come all sufferings and likewise all bad rebirths;

children.text: śubhāt sugatayaḥ sarvāḥ sarvajanmasukhāni ca || RATNA_01.21
children.translated_text: from the wholesome come all good rebirths and all the happinesses in every birth. // RATNA 1.21

children.text: nivṛttir [ 2,b ] aśubhāt kṛtsnāt pravṛttis tu śubhe sadā |
children.translated_text: Complete cessation of the unwholesome and constant engagement in the wholesome,

children.text: manasā karmaṇā vācā dharmo 'yaṃ dvividhaḥ smṛtaḥ || RATNA_01.22
children.translated_text: in mind, action, and speech — this <s>Dharma</s> is said to be twofold. // RATNA 1.22

children.text: narakapretatiryagbhyo dharmād asmād vimucyate |
children.translated_text: Through this <s>Dharma</s> one is freed from [rebirth in] the hells, the hungry ghosts, and the animals,

children.text: nṛṣu deveṣu cāpnoti sukhaśrīrājyavistarān || RATNA_01.23
children.translated_text: and among humans and gods one attains the expanses of happiness, glory, and sovereignty. // RATNA 1.23

children.text: dhyānāpramāṇārūpyais tu brahmādyasukham aśnute |
children.translated_text: Through the <s>dhyānas</s> (meditative absorptions), the <s>apramāṇas</s> (immeasurables), and the formless [attainments], one enjoys the happiness of <s>Brahmā</s> and others.

children.text: ityabhyudayadharmo 'yaṃ phalaṃ cāsya samāsataḥ || RATNA_01.24
children.translated_text: This, then, is the <s>Dharma</s> of worldly prosperity, and this is its fruit in brief. // RATNA 1.24

children.text: naiḥśreyasaḥ punar dharmaḥ sūkṣmo gambhīradarśanaḥ |
children.translated_text: But the <s>Dharma</s> of the highest good is subtle, of profound vision;

children.text: bālānāṃ [ aśrotravatām ] uktas trāsakāro jinaiḥ || RATNA_01.25
children.translated_text: spoken by the <s>Jinas</s> (Conquerors), it terrifies the childish who have not heard [it]. // RATNA 1.25

children.text: nāsmy ahaṃ na bhaviṣyāmi na me 'sti na bhaviṣyati |
children.translated_text: 'I shall not be, I shall not come to be; I do not have, I shall not have' —

children.text: iti bālasya santrāsaḥ paṇḍitasya bhayakṣayaḥ || RATNA_01.26
children.translated_text: this is the terror of the childish, and the destruction of fear for the wise. // RATNA 1.26

children.text: ahaṃkāraprasūteyaṃ mamakāropasaṃhitā |
children.translated_text: These beings, born from the ego-sense (<s>ahaṃkāra</s>), accompanied by the sense of 'mine' (<s>mamakāra</s>),

children.text: prajā prajāhitaikāntavādinā 'bhihitā khila || RATNA_01.27
children.translated_text: were declared [as such] by the One whose sole intent is the welfare of beings. // RATNA 1.27

children.text: asty ahaṃ mama cāstīti mithyaitat paramārthataḥ |
children.translated_text: 'I exist' and 'mine exists' — this is false in ultimate reality,

children.text: yathābhūtaparijñānān na bhavaty ubhayam yataḥ || RATNA_01.28
children.translated_text: since, through knowledge of things as they are, neither [of the two] arises. // RATNA 1.28

children.text: ahaṃkārodbhavāḥ skandhāḥ so 'haṃkāro 'nṛto 'rthataḥ |
children.translated_text: The <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) arise from the ego-sense, and that ego-sense is, in truth, unreal.

children.text: bījaṃ yasyānṛtaṃ tasya prarohaḥ satyataḥ kutaḥ || RATNA_01.29
children.translated_text: When the seed is unreal, how can its sprout be real? // RATNA 1.29

children.text: skandhān asatyān dṛṣṭvaivam ahaṃkāraḥ prahīyate |
children.translated_text: Having seen the <s>skandhas</s> as unreal, the ego-sense is abandoned;

children.text: ahaṃkāraprahāṇāc ca na punaḥ skandhasaṃbhavaḥ || RATNA_01.30
children.translated_text: with the abandonment of the ego-sense, the <s>skandhas</s> do not arise again. // RATNA 1.30

children.text: yathādarśam upādāya [ svamukhapratibimbakam |
children.translated_text: Just as, depending on a mirror, the reflection of one's own face

children.text: dṛśya ] te nāma tac caivam na kiṃcid api tattvataḥ || RATNA_01.31
children.translated_text: is seen — yet that [reflection] is nothing at all in reality — // RATNA 1.31

children.text: ahaṃkāras tathā skandhān upādāyopalabhyate |
children.translated_text: so too the ego-sense is apprehended depending on the <s>skandhas</s>,

children.text: na ca kaścit sa tattvena svamukhapratibimbavat || RATNA_01.32
children.translated_text: but in reality it is nothing, like the reflection of one's own face. // RATNA 1.32

children.text: yathādarśam anādāya svamukhapratibimbakam |
children.translated_text: Just as without a mirror the reflection of one's own face

children.text: na dṛśyate tathā skandhān [ 3,a ] anādāyāham ity api || RATNA_01.33
children.translated_text: is not seen, so too without the <s>skandhas</s>, [the thought] 'I' also [does not arise]. // RATNA 1.33

children.text: evaṃvidhārthaśravaṇād dharmacakṣur avāptavān |
children.translated_text: Having heard the meaning of such [teachings], the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> attained the eye of <s>Dharma</s>,

children.text: āryānanandaḥ svayaṃ caiva bhikṣubhyo 'bhīkṣṇam uktavān || RATNA_01.34
children.translated_text: and he himself spoke of it repeatedly to the <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks). // RATNA 1.34

children.text: skandhagrāho yāvad asti tāvad evāham ity api |
children.translated_text: As long as there is grasping at the <s>skandhas</s>, so long is there the [notion] 'I' as well;

children.text: ahaṃkāre sati punaḥ karma janma tataḥ punaḥ || RATNA_01.35
children.translated_text: when there is ego-sense, there is again <s>karma</s> (action), and from that, birth again. // RATNA 1.35

children.text: trivartmaitad anādyantamadhyaṃ saṃsāramaṇḍalaṃ |
children.translated_text: This threefold path, without beginning, middle, or end — this wheel of <s>saṃsāra</s>,

children.text: alātamaṇḍalaprakhyaṃ bhramaty anyonyahetukaṃ || RATNA_01.36
children.translated_text: resembling a whirling firebrand, revolves, each [element] being the cause of the others. // RATNA 1.36

children.text: svaparobhayatas tasya traikālyato 'py aprāptitaḥ |
children.translated_text: Since it is not found in oneself, in another, or in both, nor in the three times,

children.text: ahaṃkāraḥ kṣayaṃ yāti tataḥ karma ca janma ca || RATNA_01.37
children.translated_text: the ego-sense is destroyed, and thereupon <s>karma</s> and birth [as well]. // RATNA 1.37

children.text: evaṃ hetuphalotpādaṃ paśyaṃs tatkṣayaṃ eva ca |
children.translated_text: One who thus sees the arising of cause and effect, and also their destruction,

children.text: nāstitām astitāṃ caiva naiti lokasya tattvataḥ || RATNA_01.38
children.translated_text: does not arrive at either the non-existence or the existence of the world in reality. // RATNA 1.38

children.text: sarvaduḥkhakṣayaṃ dharmaṃ śrutvaivam aparīkṣakaḥ |
children.translated_text: One who, upon hearing the <s>Dharma</s> that is the destruction of all suffering, does not examine [it but]

children.text: saṃkampaty aparijñānād abhayasthānakātaraḥ || RATNA_01.39
children.translated_text: trembles through non-comprehension — such a one is fearful at the place of fearlessness. // RATNA 1.39

children.text: na bhaviṣyati nirvāṇe sarvam etan na te bhayam |
children.translated_text: 'All this will not exist in <s>nirvāṇa</s>' — let this not be a fear for you;

children.text: ucyamāna ihābhāvas tasya te kiṃ bhayaṃkaraḥ || RATNA_01.40
children.translated_text: when the non-existence [of suffering] is being spoken of here, how is that frightening to you? // RATNA 1.40

children.text: mokṣe nātmā na ca skandhā mokṣaś ced īdṛṣaḥ priyaḥ |
children.translated_text: In liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>) there is neither self (<s>ātman</s>) nor <s>skandhas</s>. If liberation of this kind is dear [to you],

children.text: ātmaskandhāpanayanaṃ kim ihaiva tavāpriyaṃ || RATNA_01.41
children.translated_text: why is the removal of self and <s>skandhas</s> displeasing to you right here [and now]? // RATNA 1.41

children.text: na cābhāvo 'pi nirvāṇaṃ kuta eva tasya bhāvatā |
children.translated_text: <s>Nirvāṇa</s> is not even non-existence — how much less could it be existence!

children.text: bhāvābhāvaparāmarśakṣayo nirvāṇam ucyate || RATNA_01.42
children.translated_text: The cessation of clinging to existence and non-existence — that is called <s>nirvāṇa</s>. // RATNA 1.42

children.text: samāsān nāstitādṛṣṭiḥ phalaṃ nāstīti karmaṇaḥ |
children.translated_text: In brief, the view of non-existence [holds that] there is no fruit of action;

children.text: apuṇyāpāyikī caiṣā mithyādṛṣṭir iti smṛtā || RATNA_01.43
children.translated_text: it is demeritorious, leading to bad rebirths, and is called wrong view (<s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>). // RATNA 1.43

children.text: samāsād astitādṛṣtiḥ phalaṃ cāstīti karmaṇām |
children.translated_text: In brief, the view of existence [holds that] there is fruit of actions;

children.text: puṇyā sugatiniṣyandā samyagdṛṣṭir iti smṛtā || RATNA_01.44
children.translated_text: it is meritorious, yielding the flow of good rebirths, and is called right view (<s>samyagdṛṣṭi</s>). // RATNA 1.44

children.text: jñāne [ 3,b ] nāstyastitāśānteḥ pāpapuṇyavyatikramaḥ |
children.translated_text: Through knowledge, when existence and non-existence are pacified, there is transcendence of sin and merit;

children.text: durgateḥ sugateś cāsmāt sa mokṣah sadbhir ucyate || RATNA_01.45
children.translated_text: and from [transcending] both bad rebirth and good rebirth — that is called liberation by the wise. // RATNA 1.45

children.text: sahetum udayaṃ paśyan nāstitām ativartate |
children.translated_text: Seeing arising as having a cause, one transcends the [view of] non-existence;

children.text: astitām api nopaiti nirodhaṃ saha hetunā || RATNA_01.46
children.translated_text: and one does not adopt the [view of] existence [either], [seeing] cessation together with its cause. // RATNA 1.46

children.text: prāgjātaḥ sahajātaś ca hetur ahetuko 'rthataḥ |
children.translated_text: A cause that is prior-born, simultaneous-born, or causeless is, in reality, [none of these],

children.text: prajñapter apratītatvād utpatteś caiva tattvataḥ || RATNA_01.47
children.translated_text: because of the [mere] convention [involved], because of its not being apprehended [as such], and because of the [non-]arising [of anything] in truth. // RATNA 1.47

children.text: asmin satīdaṃ bhavati dīrghe hrasvaṃ yathā sati |
children.translated_text: When this exists, that comes to be — just as when there is long, there is short;

children.text: [ tasyotpādād udetīdaṃ dīpotpādād yathā ] prabhā || RATNA_01.48
children.translated_text: from the arising of this, that arises — just as from the arising of a lamp, [there is] light. // RATNA 1.48

children.text: hrasve 'sati punar dīrghaṃ na bhavati svabhāvataḥ |
children.translated_text: When short does not exist, long does not exist by its own nature;

children.text: pradīpasyāpy anutpādāt prabhāyā apy asaṃbhavaḥ || RATNA_01.49
children.translated_text: and from the non-arising of the lamp, there is also the non-occurrence of light. // RATNA 1.49

children.text: evaṃ hetuphalotpādaṃ dṛṣtvā nopaiti nāstikyaṃ |
children.translated_text: Thus, seeing the arising of cause and effect, one does not arrive at nihilism,

children.text: abhyupetyāsya lokasya yāthābhūtyaṃ prapañcajam || RATNA_01.50
children.translated_text: having accepted the actuality of this world [as] born from conceptual proliferation (<s>prapañca</s>). // RATNA 1.50

children.text: nirodhaṃ ca prapañcotthaṃ yāthābhūtyād upāgataḥ |
children.translated_text: And having arrived at the actuality of cessation born from [the ending of] conceptual proliferation,

children.text: nopayāty astitāṃ tasmān mucyate 'dvayaniśritaḥ || RATNA_01.51
children.translated_text: one does not adopt [the view of] existence; therefore, one is liberated, resting in non-duality. // RATNA 1.51

children.text: durād ālokitaṃ rūpam āsannair dṛśyate sphuṭam |
children.translated_text: A form seen from afar is seen clearly by those nearby;

children.text: marīcir yadi vāri syād āsannaiḥ kiṃ na dṛśyate || RATNA_01.52
children.translated_text: if a mirage were [truly] water, why is it not seen by those nearby? // RATNA 1.52

children.text: dūrībhūtair yathābhūto loko 'yaṃ dṛśyate tathā |
children.translated_text: By those far away, this world is seen as real, just so;

children.text: na dṛśyate tadāsannair animitto marīcivat || RATNA_01.53
children.translated_text: but by those nearby [i.e., the wise] it is not seen as such — it is without basis, like a mirage. // RATNA 1.53

children.text: [ marīcis toyasadṛśī yathā nāmbo na ] cārthataḥ |
children.translated_text: A mirage resembles water — it is not water, nor is it real.

children.text: skandhās tathātmasadṛśā natmāno nāpi te 'rthataḥ || RATNA_01.54
children.translated_text: Similarly, the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) resemble a self — they are not a self, nor are they real. // RATNA 1.54

children.text: mariciṃ toyam ity etad iti matvāgato 'tra san |
children.translated_text: If, having thought 'that is water' and having gone to a mirage,

children.text: yadi nāstīti tat toyaṃ [ gṛhṇīyān mūḍha eva saḥ || RATNA_01.55
children.translated_text: one were to grasp [and say] 'that water does not exist' — that person would be a fool indeed. // RATNA 1.55

children.text: marīcipratimaṃ lo ] kam [ 4,a ] evam astīti gṛhṇataḥ |
children.translated_text: For one who grasps this world, which is like a mirage, as 'it exists' —

children.text: nāstīti cāpi moho 'yaṃ sati mohe na mucyate || RATNA_01.56
children.translated_text: and also as 'it does not exist' — this is delusion; while delusion persists, one is not liberated.

children.text: nāstiko durgatiṃ yāti sugatiṃ yāti cāstikaḥ |
children.translated_text: The nihilist goes to a bad rebirth, and the eternalist goes to a good rebirth;

children.text: yathābhūtaparijñānān mokṣam advayaniśritaḥ || RATNA_01.57
children.translated_text: through knowledge of things as they truly are, one attains liberation, resting in non-duality.

children.text: anicchan nāstitāstitve yathābhūtaparijñayā |
children.translated_text: Not desiring either non-existence or existence, through knowledge of things as they truly are,

children.text: nāstitāṃ labhate mohāt kasmān na labhate 'stitāṃ || RATNA_01.58
children.translated_text: if one arrives at non-existence through delusion, why does one not arrive at existence?

children.text: syād astidūṣaṇād asya nāstitākṣipyate 'rthataḥ |
children.translated_text: It may be argued that by refuting existence, non-existence is implied in meaning;

children.text: nāstitādūṣanād eva kasmān nākṣipyate 'stitā || RATNA_01.59
children.translated_text: but from the refutation of non-existence itself, why is existence not implied?

children.text: na pratijñā na caritaṃ na cittaṃ bodhiniśrayāt |
children.translated_text: Neither the assertion, nor the conduct, nor the mind of those who rely on awakening

children.text: nāstikatve 'rthato yeṣāṃ kathaṃ te nāstikāḥ smṛṭāḥ || RATNA_01.60
children.translated_text: constitutes nihilism in reality — how then are they regarded as nihilists?

children.text: sasāṃkhyaulūkyanirgranthapudgalaskandhavādinam |
children.translated_text: Ask the world — consisting of <s>Sāṃkhya</s>, <s>Vaiśeṣika</s>, <s>Nirgrantha</s>, and proponents of <s>pudgala</s> (person) and <s>skandha</s> (aggregates) —

children.text: pṛccha lokaṃ yadi vadaty astināstivyatikramam || RATNA_01.61
children.translated_text: whether they teach the transcendence of existence and non-existence.

children.text: dharmayautakam ity asmān nāstyastitvavyatikramam |
children.translated_text: Therefore know that the transcendence of non-existence and existence,

children.text: viddhi gaṃbhīram ity uktaṃ buddhānāṃ śāsanāmṛtam || RATNA_01.62
children.translated_text: which has <s>dharma</s> as its dowry, is declared profound — the nectar of the <s>Buddha</s>s' teaching.

children.text: vibhavaṃ naiti nāyāti na tiṣṭhaty api cakṣaṇam |
children.translated_text: The world does not go to destruction, does not come into being, and does not remain even for an instant;

children.text: traikālyavyativṛttātmā loka eva kuto 'rthataḥ || RATNA_01.63
children.translated_text: its nature transcends the three times — what then is the world, in reality?

children.text: dvayor apy āgatigatī prasthitiś ca na tattvataḥ |
children.translated_text: For both [the world and <s>nirvāṇa</s>], coming and going

children.text: lokanirvāṇayos tasmād viśeṣaḥ ka ivārthataḥ || RATNA_01.64
children.translated_text: and remaining do not exist in truth — what then is the real difference between the world and <s>nirvāṇa</s>?

children.text: sthiter abhāvād udayo nirodhaś ca na tattvataḥ |
children.translated_text: Since remaining does not exist, arising and cessation do not exist in truth;

children.text: uditaḥ sthitaś ceti niruddhaś ca kuto 'rthataḥ || RATNA_01.65
children.translated_text: how can what has arisen, remained, and ceased exist in reality?

children.text: katham aksaṇiko bhāvaḥ pariṇāmaḥ sadā yadi |
children.translated_text: How can a thing be non-momentary if it always undergoes transformation?

children.text: nāsti cet pariṇāmaḥ syād anyathātvaṃ kuto 'rthataḥ || RATNA_01.66
children.translated_text: And if there is no transformation, how can change exist in reality?

children.text: ekadeśe [ 4,b ] kṣayād vā syāt kṣaṇikaṃ sarvaśo 'pi vā |
children.translated_text: It would be momentary either through partial decay or through total decay;

children.text: vaiṣamyānupalabdheś ca dvidhāpy etad ayuktimat || RATNA_01.67
children.translated_text: but since inequality is not perceived, both views are untenable.

children.text: kṣaṇike sarvathā bhāvet kutaḥ kācit purāṇatā |
children.translated_text: If things are entirely momentary, how can there be any oldness?

children.text: sthairyād akṣaṇike cāpi kutaḥ kācit purāṇatā || RATNA_01.68
children.translated_text: And if things are permanent and non-momentary, how too can there be any oldness?

children.text: yathānto 'sti kṣaṇasyaivam ādir madhyaṃ ca kalpyatām |
children.translated_text: Just as a moment has an end, so its beginning and middle should be posited;

children.text: tryātmakatvāt kṣaṇasyaivaṃ na lokasya kṣaṇaṃ sthitiḥ || RATNA_01.69
children.translated_text: since a moment thus has a threefold nature, the world does not endure for even a moment.

children.text: ādimadhyāvasānāni c [ intyāni kṣaṇavat punaḥ |
children.translated_text: Beginning, middle, and end should be analyzed like a moment;

children.text: ādimadhyā ] vasānatvaṃ na svataḥ parato 'pi vā || RATNA_01.70
children.translated_text: beginning, middle, and end-ness arises neither from itself nor from another.

children.text: naiko 'nekapradeśatvān nāpradeśaś ca kaścana |
children.translated_text: A single thing does not exist, since it has multiple parts; nor is there anything without parts;

children.text: vinaikam api nāneko nāstitvam api cāstitām || RATNA_01.71
children.translated_text: without a single thing there is no multiplicity; and without existence there is no non-existence.

children.text: vināśāt pratipakṣād vā syād astitvasya nāstitā |
children.translated_text: Non-existence of existence would arise from destruction or from an antidote;

children.text: vināśaḥ pratipakṣo vā kathaṃ syād astyasaṃbhavāt || RATNA_01.72
children.translated_text: but how can destruction or an antidote occur when existence itself is impossible?

children.text: nirvṛtes tena lokasya nopaity ūnatvam arthataḥ |
children.translated_text: Therefore, through <s>nirvṛti</s> (cessation), the world does not in reality diminish;

children.text: antavān iti lokaś ca pṛṣṭas tuṣṇīṃ jino 'bhavat || RATNA_01.73
children.translated_text: when asked whether the world is finite, the <s>Jina</s> (Victorious One) remained silent.

children.text: sarvajña iti sarvajño budhais tenaiva gamyate |
children.translated_text: By this alone the wise understand that the <s>Jina</s> is omniscient,

children.text: yenaitad dharmagāmbhīryaṃ novācābhājane loke || RATNA_01.74
children.translated_text: since he did not teach this profound <s>dharma</s> to the unfit world.

children.text: iti naiḥśreyaso dharmo gambhīro niṣparigrahaḥ |
children.translated_text: Thus this supreme <s>dharma</s> which leads to the highest good is profound and without grasping,

children.text: anālaya ity proktaḥ saṃbuddhais tattvadarśibhiḥ || RATNA_01.75
children.translated_text: declared by the fully enlightened <s>Buddha</s>s, who see reality, to be without foundation (<s>anālaya</s>).

children.text: asmād anālayād dharmād ālayābhiratā janāḥ |
children.translated_text: From this foundationless <s>dharma</s>, people who delight in foundations,

children.text: astināstyavyatikrantā bhītā naśyanty amedhasaḥ || RATNA_01.76
children.translated_text: who have not transcended existence and non-existence, are frightened and perish — the foolish ones.

children.text: te naṣṭā nāśayanty anyān abhayasthānabhīravaḥ |
children.translated_text: Having perished, they cause others to perish — those who fear the place of fearlessness;

children.text: tathā kuru yathā rājan naṣṭair na vipranāśyase || RATNA_01.77
children.translated_text: O King, act in such a way that you are not led to ruin by the ruined.

children.text: [ 6a ] kadalī pāṭitā yadvan niḥśeṣāvayavaiḥ saha |
children.translated_text: Just as a plantain tree, when split open, is found to be nothing whatsoever along with all its parts,

children.text: na kiṃcit puruṣas tadvat pāṭitaḥ saha dhātubhiḥ || RATNA_02.01
children.translated_text: so too a person, when analyzed along with the <s>dhātu</s>s (elements), is nothing whatsoever.

children.text: sarvadharmā anātmāna ity ato bhāṣitaṃ jinaiḥ |
children.translated_text: Therefore it was declared by the <s>Jina</s>s that all <s>dharma</s>s (phenomena) are without self;

children.text: dhātuṣaṭkaṃ ca taiḥ sarvaṃ nirṇītaṃ tac ca nārthataḥ || RATNA_02.02
children.translated_text: the sixfold group of <s>dhātu</s>s (elements) was fully determined by them — and even that is not real.

children.text: naivam ātmā na cānātmā yāthābhūtyena labhyate |
children.translated_text: Thus, neither self nor non-self is obtained as it truly is;

children.text: ātmānātmakṛtadṛṣṭī varvārāsmān mahāmuniḥ || RATNA_02.03
children.translated_text: therefore the Great Sage (<s>Mahāmuni</s>) put an end to the views of self and non-self.

children.text: dṛṣṭaśruṭādyaṃ muninā na satyaṃ na mṛṣoditaṃ |
children.translated_text: What is seen, heard, and so forth was declared by the Sage to be neither true nor false;

children.text: pakṣāddhi pratipakṣaḥ syād ubhayaṃ tac ca nārthataḥ || RATNA_02.04
children.translated_text: for from a thesis an antithesis would follow, and both are not real.

children.text: iti satyānṛtātīto loko 'yaṃ paramārthataḥ |
children.translated_text: Thus this world, which transcends truth and falsehood, in the ultimate sense —

children.text: asmād eva ca tattvena nopaity asti ca nāsti ca || RATNA_02.05
children.translated_text: precisely because of this — does not in truth come to be either existent or non-existent.

children.text: yac caivaṃ sarvathā neti sarvajñas tat kathaṃ vadet |
children.translated_text: And since [the world] is in every way 'not so' — how would the Omniscient One declare that?

children.text: sāntam ity athavānantaṃ dvayaṃ vādvayam eva vā || RATNA_02.06
children.translated_text: Whether it is finite, or infinite, or both, or neither?

children.text: asaṃkhyeyā gatā buddhās tathaiṣyanty atha sāṃpratāḥ |
children.translated_text: Innumerable <s>Buddha</s>s have passed, and likewise shall come in the future, and are present now;

children.text: koṭyagraśaś ca sattvāntas tebhyas traikālyajo mataḥ || RATNA_02.07
children.translated_text: and sentient beings numbering in the tens of millions — from these arises the notion of the three times.

children.text: vṛddhihetur na lokasya kṣayas traikālyasambhavaḥ |
children.translated_text: There is no increase or decrease of the world arising from the three times;

children.text: sarvajñena kathaṃ tasya pūrvānto 'vyākṛtaḥ kṛtaḥ || RATNA_02.08
children.translated_text: why then did the Omniscient One leave its prior limit undeclared?

children.text: etat tu dharmagāmbhīryaṃ yat tad guhyaṃ pṛthagjane |
children.translated_text: This profundity of the <s>dharma</s>, which is a secret to ordinary beings,

children.text: māyopamatvaṃ lokasya buddhānāṃ śāsanāmṛtaṃ || RATNA_02.09
children.translated_text: is the illusion-like nature of the world — the nectar of the <s>Buddha</s>s' teaching.

children.text: māyāgajasya dṛśyeta yathā janmānta eva ca |
children.translated_text: Just as an illusory elephant is seen to have birth and death,

children.text: na ca kaścit sa tattvena janmāntaś caiva vidyate || RATNA_02.10
children.translated_text: yet in truth there is no such thing — neither its birth nor its death exists.

children.text: māyopamasyalokasya tathā janmānta eva ca |
children.translated_text: Likewise, of this illusion-like world, birth and death

children.text: dṛśyate paramārthena na ca janmānta eva ca || RATNA_02.11
children.translated_text: are seen, but in the ultimate sense, neither birth nor death exists.

children.text: yathā māyāgajo naiti kutaścid yāti [ 6b ] na kvacit |
children.translated_text: Just as an illusory elephant comes from nowhere and goes to nowhere,

children.text: cittamohanamātratvād bhāvatvena na tiṣṭhati || RATNA_02.12
children.translated_text: being merely a deception of the mind, it does not exist as a real entity.

children.text: tathā māyopamo loko naiti yāti na kutracit |
children.translated_text: Likewise, this illusion-like world comes from nowhere and goes to nowhere;

children.text: cittamohanamātratvād bhāvatvena na tiṣṭhati || RATNA_02.13
children.translated_text: being merely a deception of the mind, it does not exist as a real entity.

children.text: traikālyavyativṛttātmā loka evaṃ nu ko 'rthataḥ |
children.translated_text: The world, whose nature transcends the three times — what is it in reality,

children.text: yo 'sti nāsty athavāpi syād anyatra vyavahārataḥ || RATNA_02.14
children.translated_text: whether it exists, or does not exist, or might be — apart from mere convention?

children.text: catuṣprakāram ity asmāt sānto 'nanto dvayo 'dvayaḥ |
children.translated_text: Therefore, the fourfold [set of questions] — finite, infinite, both, and neither —

children.text: buddhena hetor nānyasmād ayam avyākṛtaḥ kṛtaḥ || RATNA_02.15
children.translated_text: was left undeclared by the <s>Buddha</s> for this very reason, and for no other.

children.text: śarīrāśucitā tāvan sthūlā pratyakṣagocarā |
children.translated_text: Even the impurity of the body, which is gross and within the range of direct perception,

children.text: satataṃ dṛśyamānāpi yadā citte na tiṣṭhati || RATNA_02.16
children.translated_text: though constantly seen, does not remain in the mind;

children.text: tadātisūkṣmo gambhīraḥ saddharmo 'yaṃ anālayaḥ |
children.translated_text: then how will this exceedingly subtle, profound, foundationless true <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: apratyakṣaḥ kathaṃ citte sukhenāvatariṣyati || RATNA_02.17
children.translated_text: which is beyond direct perception, easily enter the mind?

children.text: sambudhyāsmān nirvṛtto 'bhūd dharmaṃ deśayituṃ muniḥ |
children.translated_text: Knowing that this <s>dharma</s> is difficult to understand by people due to its extreme profundity,

children.text: durjñānam atigāmbhiryāj jñātvā dharmam imaṃ janaiḥ || RATNA_02.18
children.translated_text: the Sage, upon awakening, turned away from teaching the <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: vināśayati durjñāto dharmo 'yam avipaścitaṃ |
children.translated_text: When poorly understood, this <s>dharma</s> destroys the unwise,

children.text: nāstitādṛṣṭisamale yasmād asmin nimajjati || RATNA_02.19
children.translated_text: since one sinks into the mire of the view of nihilism.

children.text: aparo 'py asya durjñānān mūrkhaḥ paṇḍitamānikaḥ |
children.translated_text: Moreover, another fool, due to misunderstanding this,

children.text: pratikṣepavinaṣṭātmā yāty avīcim adhomukhaḥ || RATNA_02.20
children.translated_text: proud of being learned, having destroyed himself through rejection, falls headlong into <s>Avīci</s>.

children.text: durbhuktena yathānnena vināśam adhigacchati |
children.translated_text: Just as one who eats food badly comes to ruin,

children.text: subhuktenāyur ārogyaṃ balaṃ saukhyāni cāśnute || RATNA_02.21
children.translated_text: while one who eats well enjoys long life, health, strength, and pleasures;

children.text: durjñātena tathānena vināśam adhigacchati |
children.translated_text: so too, through misunderstanding this [<s>dharma</s>], one comes to ruin,

children.text: samyagjñātenātra sukhaṃ bodhiṃ cāpnoty anuttarāṃ || RATNA_02.22
children.translated_text: while through correct understanding, one attains happiness and unsurpassed <s>bodhi</s> (awakening).

children.text: tasmād atra pratikṣepaṃ dṛṣṭiṃ tyaktvā ca nāstikīṃ |
children.translated_text: Therefore, abandoning rejection and the nihilistic view regarding this,

children.text: saṃyagjñānaparaṃ yatnaṃ kuru [ 7a ] sarvārthasiddhaye || RATNA_02.23
children.translated_text: strive with utmost effort for correct knowledge, for the accomplishment of all aims.

children.text: dharmasyāsyāparijñānād ahaṃkāro 'nuvartate |
children.translated_text: Through non-understanding of this <s>dharma</s>, the sense of 'I' (<s>ahaṃkāra</s>) continues;

children.text: tataḥ śubhāśubhaṃ karma tato janma śubhāśubhaṃ || RATNA_02.24
children.translated_text: from that arises virtuous and non-virtuous <s>karma</s>, and from that, good and bad birth.

children.text: tasmād yāvad avijñāto dharmo 'haṃkāraśātanaḥ |
children.translated_text: Therefore, as long as this <s>dharma</s> that destroys the sense of 'I' is not understood,

children.text: dānaśīlakṣamādharme tāvad ādaravān bhava || RATNA_02.25
children.translated_text: so long be devoted to the <s>dharma</s> of generosity (<s>dāna</s>), moral conduct (<s>śīla</s>), and patience (<s>kṣamā</s>).

children.text: dharmapūrvāṇi kāryāṇi dharmamadhyāni pārthiva |
children.translated_text: O King, one whose undertakings begin with <s>dharma</s>, have <s>dharma</s> as their middle,

children.text: sādhayan dharmaniṣṭhāni neha nāmutra sīdati || RATNA_02.26
children.translated_text: and culminate in <s>dharma</s> — such a one does not suffer either here or hereafter.

children.text: dharmāt kīrtiḥ sukhaṃ caiva neha bhīr na mumūrṣataḥ |
children.translated_text: From <s>dharma</s> come fame and happiness here, no fear even at death,

children.text: paralokasukhaṃ sphītaṃ tasmād dharmaṃ sadā bhaja || RATNA_02.27
children.translated_text: and abundant happiness in the next world — therefore always practice <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: dharma eva parā nītir dharmāl loko 'nurajyate |
children.translated_text: <s>Dharma</s> alone is the highest statecraft; through <s>dharma</s> the world is won over;

children.text: rañjitena hi lokena neha nāmutra vañcyate || RATNA_02.28
children.translated_text: and by a world that has been won over, one is not deceived here or hereafter.

children.text: adharmeṇa tu yā nītis tayā loko 'parajyate |
children.translated_text: But statecraft that is based on <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness) alienates the world;

children.text: lokāparañjanāc caiva neha nāmutra nandati || RATNA_02.29
children.translated_text: and from alienating the world, one finds no joy here or hereafter.

children.text: parātisandhānaparā kaṣṭā durgatipaddhatiḥ |
children.translated_text: The wretched path of bad rebirth, aimed at deceiving others —

children.text: anarthavidyā duṣprajñair arthavidyā kathaṃ kṛtā || RATNA_02.30
children.translated_text: how is this harmful science called a 'science of profit' by the foolish?

children.text: parātisandhānaparo nītimān katham arthataḥ |
children.translated_text: How can one who is intent on deceiving others truly be called a statesman?

children.text: yena janmasahasrāṇi bahūny ātmaiva vañcyate || RATNA_02.31
children.translated_text: For through such behavior over thousands of births, it is oneself alone who is deceived.

children.text: ripor apriyam anvicchan dosāṃs tyaktvā guṇān śraya |
children.translated_text: Wishing ill upon the enemy, abandon faults and cultivate virtues;

children.text: svahitāvāptir eva tu ripos cāpy apriyaṃ bhavet || RATNA_02.32
children.translated_text: the very attainment of one's own welfare will itself be unpleasant to the enemy.

children.text: dānena priyavadyena hitenaikāthacaryayā |
children.translated_text: Through generosity, pleasant speech, beneficial conduct, and impartial treatment —

children.text: ebhir ācara lokasya dharmasyaiva ca saṅgrahaṃ || RATNA_02.33
children.translated_text: by these, practice the gathering of the world and of <s>dharma</s> itself.

children.text: viśvāsaṃ janayaty ekaṃ satyaṃ rājñāṃ yathā dṛḍhaṃ |
children.translated_text: Just as truthfulness alone generates firm trust in kings,

children.text: tathaivābhūtam apy eṣām aviśvāsakaraṃ paraṃ || RATNA_02.34
children.translated_text: so too does falsehood generate the utmost distrust in them. (RATNA_02.34)

children.text: nāvisaṃvādavat satyaṃ [ sattve ] [ 7b ] odgataṃ arthataḥ |
children.translated_text: Truth, being consistent with reality, is not deceptive; in essence it arises from [goodness],

children.text: paraikāntahitaṃ satyam ahitatvān mṛṣetarat || RATNA_02.35
children.translated_text: Truth is that which is solely beneficial to others; the opposite is falsehood, being harmful. (RATNA_02.35)

children.text: doṣān pracchādayaty ekas tyāgo rājñāṃ yathojjvalaḥ |
children.translated_text: Just as brilliant generosity alone conceals the faults of kings,

children.text: tathā kārpaṇyam apy eṣāṃ guṇasarvasvaghātakaṃ || RATNA_02.36
children.translated_text: so too does miserliness destroy the entire wealth of their virtues. (RATNA_02.36)

children.text: upaśāntasya gāmbhīryaṃ gāmbhīryād gauravaṃ paraṃ |
children.translated_text: From tranquility comes depth, from depth comes the highest dignity,

children.text: gauravād dīptir ājñā ca tasmād upaśamaṃ bhaja || RATNA_02.37
children.translated_text: from dignity comes splendor and authority — therefore cultivate <s>upaśama</s> (inner peace). (RATNA_02.37)

children.text: ahāryabuddhiḥ prājñatvād aparapratyayaḥ sthiraḥ |
children.translated_text: A king whose intellect cannot be swayed, who is wise, who does not depend on others, and who is steadfast, cannot be deceived —

children.text: nātisandhīyate rājā tasmāt prajñāparo bhava || RATNA_02.38
children.translated_text: therefore be devoted to <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom). (RATNA_02.38)

children.text: satyatyāgaśamaprajño caturbhadro narādhipaḥ |
children.translated_text: A sovereign endowed with the four excellences — truthfulness, generosity, tranquility, and wisdom —

children.text: dharmaś caturbhadra iva stūyate devamānuṣaiḥ || RATNA_02.39
children.translated_text: is praised by gods and humans, like <s>Dharma</s> itself with its four excellences. (RATNA_02.39)

children.text: nigṛhyavādibhiḥ śuddhaiḥ prajñākāruṇyanirmalaiḥ |
children.translated_text: By constantly sitting with those who are pure debaters, stainless in wisdom and compassion,

children.text: sahāsīnasya satataṃ prajñā dharmaś ca varddhate || RATNA_02.40
children.translated_text: one's <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) and <s>Dharma</s> increase. (RATNA_02.40)

children.text: durlabhāḥ pathyavaktāraḥ śrotāras tv atidurlabhāḥ |
children.translated_text: Those who speak what is beneficial are rare; listeners are even rarer;

children.text: tebhyo 'tidurlabhatamā ye pathyasyāśu kāriṇaḥ || RATNA_02.41
children.translated_text: rarer still than those are they who swiftly act upon what is beneficial. (RATNA_02.41)

children.text: pathyam apy apriyaṃ tasmāj jñātvā śīghraṃ samācara |
children.translated_text: Therefore, knowing what is beneficial even if unpleasant, practice it quickly,

children.text: pibed auṣadham apy ugram ārogyāyātmavān iva || RATNA_02.42
children.translated_text: just as a self-disciplined person drinks even bitter medicine for the sake of health. (RATNA_02.42)

children.text: jīvitārogyarājyānāṃ cintayānityatāṃ sadā |
children.translated_text: Always contemplate the impermanence of life, health, and kingship;

children.text: tataḥ saṃvegavān dharmam ekāntena prayāsyase || RATNA_02.43
children.translated_text: then, filled with <s>saṃvega</s> (spiritual urgency), you will devote yourself wholly to <s>Dharma</s>. (RATNA_02.43)

children.text: avaśyaṃ maraṇaṃ paśyan pāpād duḥkhaṃ mṛtasya ca |
children.translated_text: Seeing that death is inevitable, and that suffering follows the deceased who has done evil,

children.text: aihikena sukhenāpi na pāpaṃ kṣātum arhasi || RATNA_02.44
children.translated_text: you should not tolerate sin even for the sake of worldly pleasure. (RATNA_02.44)

children.text: kasmiṃś ced abhayaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ bhayaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ kvacit kṣaṇe |
children.translated_text: If at one moment you see safety, and at another moment you see danger,

children.text: yady ekasmin samāśvāsaḥ kim ekasmin na te bhayaṃ || RATNA_02.45
children.translated_text: if you find reassurance in the one, why do you not have fear in the other? (RATNA_02.45)

children.text: madyāt paribhavo loke kāryahānir dhanakṣayaḥ |
children.translated_text: From intoxicants come disgrace in the world, ruin of affairs, and loss of wealth;

children.text: akāryakāraṇam mohāt [ madyam tyaja tataḥ sadā ] || RATNA_02.46
children.translated_text: they cause improper actions through delusion — [therefore always abandon intoxicants]. (RATNA_02.46)

children.text: [ 15a ] adharmam anyāyyam api prāyo rājā 'nujīvibhiḥ |
children.translated_text: [A king], for the most part, even when practicing what is wrong and unjust, is praised by his dependents —

children.text: ācaran stūyate tasmāt kṛcchrād vetti kṣamā 'kṣamaṃ || RATNA_04.01
children.translated_text: therefore he finds it difficult to know what is proper and improper. (RATNA_04.01)

children.text: anyo 'pi tāvad yaḥ kaścid durvacaḥ kṣamam apriyam |
children.translated_text: Even any other person finds it hard to hear unpleasant but fitting words;

children.text: kimu rājā mahābhaumas tvaṃ mayā bhikṣuṇā satā || RATNA_04.02
children.translated_text: how much more so a king of vast dominion like you, hearing them from me, a <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk)! (RATNA_04.02)

children.text: tvatkṛtād eva tu snehāj jagatām anukampayā |
children.translated_text: Yet out of affection born from devotion to you, and out of compassion for all beings,

children.text: aham eko vadāmi tvāṃ pathyam apy apriyaṃ bhṛśaṃ || RATNA_04.03
children.translated_text: I alone tell you what is beneficial, even though exceedingly unpleasant. (RATNA_04.03)

children.text: satyaṃ ślakṣṇārthavat pathyaṃ śiṣyaḥ kāle 'nukampayā |
children.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) has said that a disciple should be told what is true, gentle in meaning, beneficial, at the right time, and with compassion —

children.text: vācya ity āha bhagavāṃs tad evam abhidhīyase || RATNA_04.04
children.translated_text: therefore you are thus addressed. (RATNA_04.04)

children.text: akrodhe satyavākye ca ślāghyamāṇo yadi sthitaḥ |
children.translated_text: If, being praised for non-anger and truthful speech, you remain steadfast,

children.text: śravyaṃ samparigṛhṇīyāt sattoyaṃ snāpyamānavat || RATNA_04.05
children.translated_text: you will accept what is worth hearing, like one being bathed with water. (RATNA_04.05)

children.text: tasya me vadato vākyaṃ tvam ihāmutra ca kṣamaṃ |
children.translated_text: Understanding that these words of mine are fitting both here and hereafter,

children.text: jñātvā kuru hitāyedam ātmano jagato 'pi ca || RATNA_04.06
children.translated_text: act upon them for the benefit of yourself and the world as well. (RATNA_04.06)

children.text: yācakebhyaḥ purā dānāt prāpyārthāṃś cen na dāsyasi |
children.translated_text: If, having obtained wealth, you will not give to supplicants before [death takes it],

children.text: akṛtajñatvalobhābhyāṃ nārthān punar avāpsyasi || RATNA_04.07
children.translated_text: through ingratitude and greed you will not obtain wealth again. (RATNA_04.07)

children.text: iha pathy adanaṃ loke na vahaty abhṛto bhṛtaḥ |
children.translated_text: In this world, an unpaid servant does not carry loads on the road;

children.text: yācakas tv abhṛto 'mutra hīnaḥ śataguṇadvahaḥ || RATNA_04.08
children.translated_text: but a supplicant, though unpaid, carries a hundredfold reward in the next life, even for the lowly. (RATNA_04.08)

children.text: udāracittaḥ satataṃ bhavodārakriyārataḥ |
children.translated_text: One who is always noble-minded and delights in noble deeds of existence —

children.text: udārakarmaṇaḥ sarvam udāraṃ jāyate phalam || RATNA_04.09
children.translated_text: for one of noble actions, all fruits arise as noble. (RATNA_04.09)

children.text: manorathair api klībair anālīḍhaṃ narādhipaiḥ |
children.translated_text: What has not been attained even in fantasy by feeble-minded kings —

children.text: kuru dharmāspadaṃ śrīmat khyātaṃ ratnatrayāspadam || RATNA_04.10
children.translated_text: create a splendid seat of <s>Dharma</s>, renowned as a seat of the <s>Ratnatraya</s> (Three Jewels). (RATNA_04.10)

children.text: sāmantarājaromāñcakaraṃ dharmāspadaṃ na yat |
children.translated_text: A seat of <s>Dharma</s> that does not cause the hair of vassal kings to stand on end —

children.text: mṛtyasyāpy apraśasyatvād rājaṃs tad akṛtaṃ varam || RATNA_04.11
children.translated_text: since even death is not praiseworthy, O king, it is better that such a thing not be made. (RATNA_04.11)

children.text: atyaudāryād [ 15b ] udārāṇāṃ vismayotsāhavardhaṇam |
children.translated_text: Through supreme generosity, increasing the wonder and enthusiasm of the noble,

children.text: utsāhaghnaṃ ca mandānāṃ sarvasvenāpi kāraya || RATNA_04.12
children.translated_text: and crushing the enthusiasm of the base — accomplish this even at the cost of everything you possess. (RATNA_04.12)

children.text: utsṛjyāmutra gantavyaṃ sarvasvam avaśena te |
children.translated_text: You must depart to the next world, inevitably leaving behind all possessions;

children.text: dharme niyuktaṃ yāty eva purastāt sarvam eva tat || RATNA_04.13
children.translated_text: but all that is directed toward <s>Dharma</s> goes before you. (RATNA_04.13)

children.text: sarvasvaṃ pūrvanṛpateḥ nṛpasya vaśam āgataṃ |
children.translated_text: All the wealth of a former king has come into the possession of the next king —

children.text: kiṃ pūrvakasya dharmāya sukhāya yaśase 'pi vā || RATNA_04.14
children.translated_text: of what use was it to the former king for <s>Dharma</s>, happiness, or fame? (RATNA_04.14)

children.text: bhuktād arthād iha sukhaṃ dattāt pāratrikaṃ sukham |
children.translated_text: From wealth enjoyed comes happiness in this life; from wealth given comes happiness in the next;

children.text: abhuktādattanaṣṭatvād duḥkham eva kutaḥ sukhaṃ || RATNA_04.15
children.translated_text: from wealth neither enjoyed nor given, which is merely lost — there is only suffering; whence happiness? (RATNA_04.15)

children.text: vinaśyan sacivair dātum asvātantryān na śakyasi |
children.translated_text: When you are perishing, your ministers will be unable to give on your behalf, lacking autonomy,

children.text: āpatichedaniḥsnehair navarājapriyaiṣibhiḥ || RATNA_04.16
children.translated_text: for they cut ties in adversity, are devoid of loyalty, and seek to please the new king. (RATNA_04.16)

children.text: sarvasvenāpy ataḥ svasthaḥ śīghraṃ dharmāspadaṃ kuru |
children.translated_text: Therefore, while still in good health, quickly establish a seat of <s>Dharma</s> even with all your possessions,

children.text: mṛtyupratyayamadhyasthaḥ pravātasthapradīpavat || RATNA_04.17
children.translated_text: for you stand in the midst of causes of death, like a lamp placed in the wind. (RATNA_04.17)

children.text: dharmādhikārā ye cānye pūrvarājapravartitāḥ |
children.translated_text: Those other religious foundations that were established by former kings —

children.text: devadroṇyādayas te 'pi pravartyantāṃ yathā sthitāḥ || RATNA_04.18
children.translated_text: <s>devadroṇī</s> (sacred groves) and the like — let them continue to function as they were. (RATNA_04.18)

children.text: ahiṃsakaiḥ śubhācārair vratasthair atithipriyaiḥ |
children.translated_text: Let them be served by those who are non-violent, of pure conduct, observing vows, hospitable to guests,

children.text: sarvakṣamair akalahair bhajyeraṃs taiḥ sado(dya)taiḥ || RATNA_04.19
children.translated_text: forbearing toward all, free from quarrels, and always diligent. (RATNA_04.19)

children.text: andhavyādhitahīnāṅgadīnānāthavanīpakāḥ |
children.translated_text: The blind, the sick, the maimed, the destitute, the helpless, and the homeless —

children.text: te 'py annapānaṃ sāmyena labherann avighaṭṭitāḥ || RATNA_04.20
children.translated_text: let them all receive food and drink equally, without obstruction. (RATNA_04.20)

children.text: anarthīnām api satāṃ dhārmikāṇāṃ anugrahān |
children.translated_text: Even to virtuous and righteous people who have not asked,

children.text: apy anyarājyasaṃsthānām anurūpān pravarttaya || RATNA_04.21
children.translated_text: extend appropriate favors, even to those dwelling in other kingdoms. (RATNA_04.21)

children.text: sarvadharmādhikāreṣu dharmādhikṛtam utthitaṃ |
children.translated_text: In all religious foundations, appoint a superintendent of <s>Dharma</s> who is energetic,

children.text: alubdhaṃ paṇḍitaṃ dharmyaṃ kuru teṣām abādhakaṃ || RATNA_04.22
children.translated_text: free from greed, learned, righteous — and make him one who does not oppress them. (RATNA_04.22)

children.text: nītijñān dhārmikān snigdhān śucīn bhaktān akātarān |
children.translated_text: Appoint as ministers those who are versed in statecraft, righteous, affectionate, honest, loyal, courageous,

children.text: kulinān śīlasampannān [ 16a ] kṛtajñān sacivān kuru || RATNA_04.23
children.translated_text: of noble birth, endowed with good character, and grateful. (RATNA_04.23)

children.text: akṣudrāṃs tyāginaḥ śūrān snigdhān sambhoginaḥ sthirān |
children.translated_text: Appoint as military commanders those who are not petty, generous, brave, affectionate, sharing,

children.text: kuru nityāpramattāṃs ca dhārmikān daṇḍanāyakān || RATNA_04.24
children.translated_text: steadfast, always vigilant, and righteous. (RATNA_04.24)

children.text: dharmaśīlān śucīn dakṣān kāryajñān śāstrakovidān |
children.translated_text: Appoint as officials those who are virtuous in conduct, honest, capable, who know their duties, are learned in the <s>śāstras</s> (treatises),

children.text: kṛtavṛttīn samān snigdhān vṛddhān adhikṛtan kuru || RATNA_04.25
children.translated_text: are salaried, impartial, affectionate, and experienced. (RATNA_04.25)

children.text: pratimāsaṃ ca tebhyas tvaṃ sarvam āyavyayaṃ śṛṇu |
children.translated_text: Every month, hear from them the complete account of income and expenditure;

children.text: śrutvā dharmādhikārādyaṃ kāryaṃ sarvaṃ svayaṃ vada || RATNA_04.26
children.translated_text: having heard, personally direct all affairs, beginning with the religious foundations. (RATNA_04.26)

children.text: dharmārthaṃ yadi te rājyaṃ na kīrtyarthaṃ na kāmataḥ |
children.translated_text: If your kingdom is for the sake of <s>Dharma</s>, not for fame nor out of desire,

children.text: tataḥ saphalam atyartham anarthārtham ato 'nyathā || RATNA_04.27
children.translated_text: then it is exceedingly fruitful; otherwise it is for the sake of what is worthless. (RATNA_04.27)

children.text: parasparāmiṣībhūte loke 'smin prāyaśo nṛpa |
children.translated_text: In this world where beings have mostly become prey to one another, O king,

children.text: yathā rājyaṃ ca dharmaś ca bhavet tava tathā śṛṇu || RATNA_04.28
children.translated_text: hear how you may have both kingship and <s>Dharma</s>. (RATNA_04.28)

children.text: jñānavṛddhā kule jātā nyāyajñāḥ pāpabhīravaḥ |
children.translated_text: Let there always be assembled around you many advisors who are advanced in knowledge, born of good family, who know justice, and who fear sin —

children.text: sametā bahavo nityaṃ santu te kāryadarśinaḥ || RATNA_04.29
children.translated_text: as those who oversee affairs. (RATNA_04.29)

children.text: daṇḍabandhaprahārādīn kuryus te nyāyato 'pi cet |
children.translated_text: Even if they carry out punishments, imprisonment, beatings, and the like according to justice,

children.text: kārunyārdraḥ sadā bhūtvā tvam anugrahavān bhava || RATNA_04.30
children.translated_text: you should always remain tender with compassion and be gracious. (RATNA_04.30)

children.text: hitāyaiva tvayā cittam unnāmyaṃ sarvadehinām |
children.translated_text: O king, your mind should be directed toward the welfare of all living beings,

children.text: kāruṇyāt satataṃ rājaṃs tīvrapāpakṛtām api || RATNA_04.31
children.translated_text: with constant compassion, even toward those who have committed grievous sins. (RATNA_04.31)

children.text: tīvrapāpeṣu hiṃsreṣu kṛpā kāryā viśeṣataḥ |
children.translated_text: Especially toward those who commit terrible sins and are violent, compassion should be shown,

children.text: ta eva hi kṛpāsthānam hatāmāno mahātmanām || RATNA_04.32
children.translated_text: for they indeed are the proper objects of compassion for great souls, being ones whose dignity is destroyed. (RATNA_04.32)

children.text: pratyahaṃ pañcarātram vā baddhān kṣīnān vimocaya |
children.translated_text: Every day, or every five days, release prisoners who are weakened;

children.text: śeṣān api yathāyogaṃ mā kāṃścit naiva mocaya || RATNA_04.33
children.translated_text: release the rest also as appropriate — never fail to release any at all. (RATNA_04.33)

children.text: yeṣv amokṣaṇacittaṃ te jāyate teṣv asaṃvaraḥ |
children.translated_text: Toward those for whom you have no intention of releasing, there arises a lack of moral restraint;

children.text: tasmād asaṃvarāt pāpam ajasram upacīyate || RATNA_04.34
children.translated_text: from that lack of restraint, sin accumulates ceaselessly. (RATNA_04.34)

children.text: [ 16b ] yāvac ca na vimucyeraṃs tāvat syuḥ sukhabandhanāḥ |
children.translated_text: As long as they are not released, let them be held in comfortable confinement,

children.text: nāpitasnānapānānnabhaiṣajyavasanānvitāḥ || RATNA_04.35
children.translated_text: provided with barbers, baths, drinks, food, medicine, and clothing. (RATNA_04.35)

children.text: apātreṣv iva putreṣu pātrīkaraṇakāṅkṣayā |
children.translated_text: Just as unworthy sons are disciplined with the wish to make them worthy,

children.text: kāruṇy [ āt tāḍanam kāryaṃ na dveṣān ] nārthalipsayā || RATNA_04.36
children.translated_text: [punishment should be administered] out of compassion, [not out of hatred] nor out of desire for gain. (RATNA_04.36)

children.text: vimṛśya saṃyag vijñāya praduṣṭān ghātakān api |
children.translated_text: Having carefully examined and ascertained the case, even convicted murderers

children.text: ahatvā 'pīḍayitvā ca kuru nirviṣayān narān || RATNA_04.37
children.translated_text: should not be killed or tortured, but rather banished from the realm. (RATNA_04.37)

children.text: svatantraḥ paśya sarvaṃ ca viṣayaṃ cāracakṣuṣā |
children.translated_text: Personally oversee everything, and survey the realm through the eyes of spies;

children.text: nityāpramattaḥ smṛtimān kuru kāryaṃ ca dhārmikaṃ || RATNA_04.38
children.translated_text: always vigilant and mindful, carry out your duties righteously. (RATNA_04.38)

children.text: pradānamānasatkārair guṇasthān satataṃ bhaja |
children.translated_text: Always honor those who are established in virtue through gifts, respect, and reverence;

children.text: udārair anurūpais tu śeṣān api yathāvidhi || RATNA_04.39
children.translated_text: and attend to the rest also, appropriately and according to proper custom, with generosity. (RATNA_04.39)

children.text: sammānasphītakusumaḥ sampradānamahāphalaḥ |
children.translated_text: The royal tree, blossoming with the flowers of honor, bearing the great fruit of gifts,

children.text: rājavṛkṣaḥ kṣamācchāyaḥ sevyate bhṛtyaprakṣibhiḥ || RATNA_04.40
children.translated_text: shaded by the canopy of forbearance, is frequented by the birds that are his servants. (RATNA_04.40)

children.text: tyāgaśīlamayo rājā tejasvī bhavati priyaḥ |
children.translated_text: A king composed of generosity and good character is powerful and beloved,

children.text: śarkarāmodako yadvad elāmaricakarkaśaḥ || RATNA_04.41
children.translated_text: just as a sugar candy, though hard with cardamom and pepper, is [still sweet]. (RATNA_04.41)

children.text: mātsyanyāyaś ca te naivaṃ nyāyād rājyaṃ bhaviṣyati |
children.translated_text: Thus, the law of the fishes shall not prevail, and your kingdom shall be governed by justice;

children.text: na cānyāyo na vā 'dharmo dharmaś caivaṃ bhaviṣyati || RATNA_04.42
children.translated_text: there shall be neither injustice nor unrighteousness, and <s>Dharma</s> alone shall prevail. (RATNA_04.42)

children.text: paralokāt tvayā rājyaṃ nānītaṃ nāpi neṣyasi |
children.translated_text: You did not bring your kingdom from the next world, nor will you take it there.

children.text: dharmāt prāptam ato 'syārthe nādharmaṃ kartum arhasi || RATNA_04.43
children.translated_text: Since it was obtained through <s>dharma</s>, you should not commit <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness) for its sake.

children.text: rājyena bhāṇḍamūlyena duḥkhabhāṇḍaparamparām |
children.translated_text: O King, strive so that with the merchandise-price of your kingdom,

children.text: rājan yathā nārjayasi prayatnaḥ kriyatāṃ tathā || RATNA_04.44
children.translated_text: you do not purchase a succession of loads of suffering.

children.text: rājyena bhāṇḍamūlyena rājyabhāṇḍaparamparāṃ |
children.translated_text: O King, strive so that with the merchandise-price of your kingdom,

children.text: rājan yathā nirviśasi prayatnaḥ kriyatāṃ tathā || RATNA_04.45
children.translated_text: you invest in a succession of [further] royal merchandise.

children.text: caturdvīpām api prāpya pṛthivīṃ cakravartinaḥ [ 17a ] |
children.translated_text: Even having obtained the earth with its four continents, a <s>cakravartin</s> (universal monarch)

children.text: śārīraṃ mānasaṃ caiva sukhadvayam idaṃ matam || RATNA_04.46
children.translated_text: is considered to have only two kinds of happiness: bodily and mental.

children.text: duḥkhapratikriyāmātraṃ śārīraṃ vedanāsukhaṃ |
children.translated_text: Bodily pleasure of sensation is merely the counteraction of pain;

children.text: saṃjñāmayaṃ mānasaṃ tu kevalaṃ kaplpanākṛtaṃ || RATNA_04.47
children.translated_text: mental [pleasure] is merely conceptual — produced by imagination alone.

children.text: duḥkhapratikriyāmātraṃ kalpanāmātram eva ca |
children.translated_text: Merely the counteraction of pain and merely imagination —

children.text: lokasya sukhasarvasvaṃ vyartham etad ato 'rthataḥ || RATNA_04.48
children.translated_text: this, the entire wealth of happiness of the world, is therefore purposeless in reality.

children.text: dvīpadeśapurāvāsapradeśasānavāsasāṃ |
children.translated_text: Of those dwelling on continents, countries, cities, houses, regions, and beds,

children.text: śayyā 'nnapānahastyastyaśvastrīṇāṃ caikaikabhogyatā || RATNA_04.49
children.translated_text: only one at a time can be enjoyed among beds, food, drink, elephants, horses, and women.

children.text: yadā ca yatra cittaṃ syāt tadānena sukhaṃ kila |
children.translated_text: Whenever and wherever the mind is [engaged], then there is said to be happiness from that [alone];

children.text: śeṣāṇām amanaskārāt teṣāṃ vyarthatvam arthataḥ || RATNA_04.50
children.translated_text: the remaining ones, being unattended to by the mind, are purposeless in reality.

children.text: viṣayān pañcabhiḥ pañca cakṣurādibhir indriyaiḥ |
children.translated_text: When one grasps the five sense-objects with the five sense-organs — eye and the rest —

children.text: na kalpayati yed gṛhṇan nāsmāt teṣu tadā sukhaṃ || RATNA_04.51
children.translated_text: one does not conceptualize [them all simultaneously]; therefore there is no happiness in those [remaining ones] at that time.

children.text: jānīte viṣayaṃ yaṃ yaṃ yena yenendriyeṇa ca |
children.translated_text: Whatever sense-object one cognizes with whatever sense-organ,

children.text: tadā na śeṣaiḥ śeṣāṇi vyarthāny eva yatas tadā || RATNA_04.52
children.translated_text: at that time the remaining [objects] through the remaining [organs] are simply purposeless.

children.text: indriyair upalabdhasya viṣayasyākṛtiṃ manaḥ |
children.translated_text: The mind, having apprehended the form of a sense-object perceived by the senses,

children.text: upalabhya vyatītasya kalpayan manyate sukhaṃ || RATNA_04.53
children.translated_text: constructs [it] as past and considers [it] to be happiness.

children.text: ekam arthaṃ vijānāti yady apy ekam ihendriyaṃ |
children.translated_text: Even if one sense-organ cognizes one object here,

children.text: tad apy arthaṃ vinā vyarthaṃ vyartho 'rtho 'pi ca tad vinā || RATNA_04.54
children.translated_text: that [organ] too is purposeless without the object, and the object is also purposeless without it.

children.text: pratītya mātāpitarau yathoktaḥ putrasambhavaḥ |
children.translated_text: Just as the birth of a son is said to depend on mother and father,

children.text: cakṣūrūpe pratītyaivam ukto vijñānasaṃbhavah || RATNA_04.55
children.translated_text: so too the arising of <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) is said to depend on the eye and form.

children.text: atītānāgatā vyarthāḥ viṣayāḥ sārdham indriyaiḥ |
children.translated_text: Past and future sense-objects, together with the sense-organs, are purposeless;

children.text: taddvayānatiriktatvād vyarthā ye 'pi ca sāmpratāḥ || RATNA_04.56
children.translated_text: and since [present objects] are not different from those two [past and future], even present ones are also purposeless.

children.text: alātacakraṃ gṛhṇāti yathā cakṣur viparyayāt |
children.translated_text: Just as the eye perceives a whirling firebrand [as a circle] through error,

children.text: tathendriyāṇi [ 17b ] gṛhṇanti viṣayān sāmpratān iva || RATNA_04.57
children.translated_text: so the sense-organs grasp sense-objects as if they were present.

children.text: indriyāṇīndriyārthāś ca pañcabhūtamayā matāḥ |
children.translated_text: The sense-organs and sense-objects are held to be composed of the five elements;

children.text: pratisvaṃ bhūtavaiyarthyād eṣāṃ vyarthatvam arthataḥ || RATNA_04.58
children.translated_text: since each element is itself purposeless, these [senses and objects] are also purposeless in reality.

children.text: nirindhano 'gnir bhūtānāṃ vinirbhāge prasajyate |
children.translated_text: When the elements are separated, fire without fuel would follow [as an absurdity];

children.text: saṃparke lakṣaṇābhāvaḥ śeṣeṣv apy eṣa nirṇayaḥ || RATNA_04.59
children.translated_text: when combined, the defining characteristics are absent — the same conclusion applies to the remaining [elements].

children.text: evaṃ dvidhāpi bhūtānāṃ vyarthatvāt saṅgatir vṛthā |
children.translated_text: Thus, since the elements are purposeless in both ways [separated and combined], their combination is in vain;

children.text: vyarthatvāt saṅgateś caivaṃ rūpaṃ vyartham ato 'rthataḥ || RATNA_04.60
children.translated_text: and since the combination is purposeless, form too is purposeless in reality.

children.text: vijñānavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskārāṇām ca sarvaśaḥ |
children.translated_text: Of <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness), <s>vedanā</s> (feeling), <s>saṃjñā</s> (perception),

children.text: pratyekam ātmavaiyarthyād vaiyarthyaṃ paramārthataḥ || RATNA_04.61
children.translated_text: and <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations) — since each is individually purposeless, [they are all] purposeless in the ultimate sense.

children.text: sukhābhimāno duḥkhasya pratīkāre yathārthataḥ |
children.translated_text: Just as the notion of happiness in the counteraction of pain is [only] conventional in reality,

children.text: tathā duhkhābhimāno 'pi sukhasya pratighātajaḥ || RATNA_04.62
children.translated_text: so too the notion of pain arises from the obstruction of happiness.

children.text: sukhe saṃyogatṛṣṇaivaṃ naiḥsvābhāvyāt prahīyate |
children.translated_text: Thus the craving for union with happiness is abandoned because of [happiness's] lack of intrinsic nature,

children.text: duḥkhe viyogatṛṣṇā ca paśyatāṃ muktir ity ataḥ || RATNA_04.63
children.translated_text: and the craving for separation from suffering [is also abandoned]; therefore, for those who see [this], there is liberation.

children.text: kaḥ paśyatīti cec cittaṃ vyavahāreṇa kathyate |
children.translated_text: If one asks, 'Who sees?' — conventionally, it is called 'mind';

children.text: na hi caittaṃ vinā cittaṃ vyarthatvān na saheṣyate || RATNA_04.64
children.translated_text: but since mind does not exist apart from mental factors, it will not be maintained [as ultimately real] because of its purposelessness.

children.text: vyartham evaṃ jagan matvā yāthābhūtyān nirāspadaḥ |
children.translated_text: Having thus understood the world as purposeless, in accordance with reality one becomes free of any ground,

children.text: nirvāti nirupādāno nirupādānavahnivat || RATNA_04.65
children.translated_text: and one is extinguished without attachment, like a fire without fuel.

children.text: bodhisattvo 'pi dṛṣṭvaivaṃ sambodhau niyato mataḥ |
children.translated_text: A <s>bodhisattva</s> too, having seen thus, is considered to be determined toward perfect awakening;

children.text: kevalaṃ tv asya kāruṇyād ābodher bhavasaṃtatiḥ || RATNA_04.66
children.translated_text: but it is solely through compassion that the continuity of existence [continues] until enlightenment.

children.text: bodhisattvasya saṃbhāro mahāyāne tathāgataiḥ |
children.translated_text: The accumulation [of merit and knowledge] of a <s>bodhisattva</s> has been taught by the <s>Tathāgatas</s>

children.text: nirdiṣṭaḥ sa tu sammūḍhaiḥ pradviṣṭaiś caiva nindyate || RATNA_04.67
children.translated_text: in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>; but it is reviled by those who are deluded and hostile.

children.text: guṇadoṣānabhijño vā doṣasaṃjñī guṇeṣu vā |
children.translated_text: One who does not recognize virtues and faults, or who perceives faults in virtues,

children.text: athavāpi guṇadveṣī mahāyānasya nindakaḥ || RATNA_04.68
children.translated_text: or who is hostile to virtues — such a one is a detractor of the <s>Mahāyāna</s>.

children.text: paropaghātino [ 18a ] doṣān parānugrahiṇo guṇān |
children.translated_text: Knowing that harming others constitutes faults and benefiting others constitutes virtues,

children.text: jñātvocyate guṇadveṣī mahāyānasya nindakaḥ || RATNA_04.69
children.translated_text: one who is hostile to virtues is called a detractor of the <s>Mahāyāna</s>.

children.text: yat svārthanirapekṣatvāt parāthaikarasapriyaṃ |
children.translated_text: Since it is indifferent to self-interest and delights solely in the welfare of others,

children.text: guṇākaraṃ mahāyānaṃ tad dveṣī tena dahyate || RATNA_04.70
children.translated_text: the <s>Mahāyāna</s> is a mine of virtues — one who is hostile to it is burned by that [hostility].

children.text: śrāddho 'pi durgṛhītena dviṣyāt kruddho 'thavetaraḥ |
children.translated_text: Even a faithful person might, through misunderstanding, become hostile [to the <s>Mahāyāna</s>]; or an angry person, being different [in disposition, might do so].

children.text: śrāddho 'pi dagdha ity uktaḥ kā cintā dveṣabandhure || RATNA_04.71
children.translated_text: Even a faithful person is said to be burned [by such hostility]; what then of one who is firmly bound to hatred?

children.text: viṣeṇāpi viṣaṃ hanyād yathaivoktaṃ cikitsakaiḥ |
children.translated_text: Just as physicians have said that poison may be counteracted by poison,

children.text: duḥkhenāpy ahitaṃ hanyād ity ukte kiṃ virudhyate || RATNA_04.72
children.translated_text: what contradiction is there in saying that what is harmful may be destroyed even through suffering?

children.text: manaḥpūrvaṅgamā dharmā manaḥśreṣṭhā iti śruteḥ |
children.translated_text: Since it is heard that "mental states are forerunners, mind is supreme,"

children.text: hitaṃ hitamanāḥ kurvan duḥkenāpy ahitaṃ kathaṃ || RATNA_04.73
children.translated_text: how can one doing what is beneficial with a beneficial mind be doing harm, even through suffering?

children.text: duḥkham apy āyatīpathyaṃ kāryaṃ kimu sukhaṃ hitaṃ |
children.translated_text: Even painful [action], if wholesome for the future, should be done — how much more so pleasant action that is beneficial?

children.text: ātmanaś ca pareṣāṃ ca dharma eṣa sanātanaḥ || RATNA_04.74
children.translated_text: This is the eternal <s>dharma</s> for both oneself and others.

children.text: mātrāsukhaparityāgāt paścāc ced vipulaṃ sukhaṃ |
children.translated_text: If, after abandoning a small pleasure, there follows abundant happiness,

children.text: tyajen mātrāsukhaṃ dhīraḥ saṃpaśyan vipulaṃ sukhaṃ || RATNA_04.75
children.translated_text: the wise one should abandon the small pleasure, seeing the abundant happiness [ahead].

children.text: na mṛṣyate ca yady etat kaṭubhaiṣajyadāyinaḥ |
children.translated_text: And if this [argument] is not tolerated, then the giver of bitter medicine

children.text: tataś cikitsakādyāś ca hatā naivaṃ ca yujyate || RATNA_04.76
children.translated_text: [and] physicians and others would be destroyed [i.e., condemned] — and that is simply not right.

children.text: apathyam api yad dṛṣṭaṃ tat pathyaṃ paṇḍitaiḥ kvacit |
children.translated_text: Even what is observed to be unwholesome is considered wholesome by the wise in certain cases;

children.text: utsargaś cāpavādaś ca sarvaśāstreṣu śaṃsyate || RATNA_04.77
children.translated_text: general rules and exceptions are praised in all <s>śāstras</s> (treatises).

children.text: karuṇāpūrvakāḥ sarve niṣyandā jñānanirmalāḥ |
children.translated_text: Where all outflows are preceded by compassion, purified by knowledge,

children.text: uktā yatra mahāyāne kas tan nindet sacetanaḥ || RATNA_04.78
children.translated_text: are taught in the <s>Mahāyāna</s> — what conscious person would revile that?

children.text: atyaudāryātigāmbhīryād viṣaṇṇair akṛtātmabhiḥ |
children.translated_text: Due to its extreme generosity and extreme profundity, the <s>Mahāyāna</s> is nowadays

children.text: nindyate 'dya mahāyānaṃ mohāt svaparavairibhiḥ || RATNA_04.79
children.translated_text: reviled through delusion by those who are dejected, untrained — enemies of themselves and others.

children.text: dānaśīlakṣamāvīryadhyānaprajñākṛpātmakaṃ [ 18b ] |
children.translated_text: The <s>Mahāyāna</s> is of the nature of <s>dāna</s> (giving), <s>śīla</s> (morality), <s>kṣamā</s> (patience), <s>vīrya</s> (vigor),

children.text: mahāyānam atas tasmin kasmād durbhāṣitaṃ vacaḥ || RATNA_04.80
children.translated_text: <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), and <s>kṛpā</s> (compassion); why then should ill words be spoken against it?

children.text: parārtho dānaśīlābhyāṃ kṣāntyā vīryeṇa cātmanaḥ |
children.translated_text: Through <s>dāna</s> (giving) and <s>śīla</s> (morality) the welfare of others [is accomplished]; through <s>kṣānti</s> (patience) and <s>vīrya</s> (vigor), one's own [welfare];

children.text: dhyānaṃ prajñā ca mokṣāya mahāyānārthasaṃgrahaḥ || RATNA_04.81
children.translated_text: <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) and <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) are for liberation — this is the summary of the meaning of the <s>Mahāyāna</s>.

children.text: parā [ tmahita ] mokṣārthāḥ saṃkṣepād buddhaśāsanaṃ |
children.translated_text: The aims of benefit to others, benefit to oneself, and liberation — in brief, these are the teaching of the <s>Buddha</s>;

children.text: te saṭpāramitāgarbhās tasmād bauddham idaṃ vacaḥ || RATNA_04.82
children.translated_text: they are contained in the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections); therefore this is the word of the <s>Buddha</s>.

children.text: puṇyajñānamayo yatra buddhair bodher mahāpathaḥ |
children.translated_text: Where the great path to enlightenment, consisting of merit and knowledge,

children.text: deśitas tan mahāyānam ajñānād vai na dṛśyate || RATNA_04.83
children.translated_text: has been taught by the <s>Buddhas</s> — that is the <s>Mahāyāna</s>; through ignorance indeed it is not perceived.

children.text: kham ivācintyaguṇatvād ukto 'cintyaguṇo jinaḥ |
children.translated_text: Just as space is said to have inconceivable qualities, so the <s>Jina</s> (Conqueror) is said to have inconceivable qualities;

children.text: mahāyāne yato buddhamāhātmyaṃ kṣamyatām idam || RATNA_04.84
children.translated_text: since the greatness of the <s>Buddha</s> is [taught] in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, let this be accepted.

children.text: āryaśāradvatasyāpi śīlamātre 'py agocaraḥ |
children.translated_text: Even the morality alone of the venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s> (<s>Śāriputra</s>) lies beyond the scope [of ordinary beings];

children.text: yasmāt tad buddhamāhātmyam acintyaṃ kiṃ na mṛṣyate || RATNA_04.85
children.translated_text: since that greatness of the <s>Buddha</s> is inconceivable, why is it not accepted?

children.text: anutpādo mahāyāne pareṣāṃ śūnyātā kṣayaḥ |
children.translated_text: Non-arising is [taught] in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>; in the other [vehicle], <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) is [taught as] cessation.

children.text: kṣayānutpādāyoś caikyam arthataḥ kṣamyatāṃ yataḥ || RATNA_04.86
children.translated_text: Since cessation and non-arising are the same in meaning, let this be accepted.

children.text: śūnyatābuddhamāhātmyam evaṃ yuktyānupaśyatāṃ |
children.translated_text: For those who thus examine <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) and the greatness of the <s>Buddha</s> through reasoning,

children.text: mahāyānetaroktāni na sameyuḥ kathaṃ satāṃ || RATNA_04.87
children.translated_text: how would the teachings stated in the <s>Mahāyāna</s> and the other [vehicle] not accord for the wise?

children.text: tathāgatābhisandhyoktāny asukhaṃ jñātum ity ataḥ |
children.translated_text: Since the statements made with hidden intention by the <s>Tathāgatas</s> are difficult to understand,

children.text: ekayānatriyānoktād ātmā rakṣya upekṣayā || RATNA_04.88
children.translated_text: one should protect oneself through equanimity regarding the teaching of one vehicle and three vehicles.

children.text: upekṣayā hi nāpuṇyam dveṣāt pāpaṃ kutaḥ śubhaṃ |
children.translated_text: For through equanimity there is no demerit; through hatred there is sin — whence any good?

children.text: mahāyāne yato dveṣo nātmakāmaiḥ kṛto 'rhati || RATNA_04.89
children.translated_text: Since hatred toward the <s>Mahāyāna</s> [leads to sin], it should not be indulged in by those who love themselves.

children.text: na bodhisattvapraṇidhir na caryāpariṇāmanā |
children.translated_text: The aspiration (<s>praṇidhi</s>) of a <s>bodhisattva</s>, nor the dedication of practice,

children.text: uktāḥ śrāvakayāne 'smād bodhisattvaḥ kutas tataḥ || RATNA_04.90
children.translated_text: are taught in the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s>; how then could a <s>bodhisattva</s> [arise] from that?

children.text: adhiṣṭhānāni noktāni [ 19a ] bodhisattvasya bodhaye |
children.translated_text: The foundations (<s>adhiṣṭhānas</s>) for a <s>bodhisattva's</s> awakening have not been taught

children.text: buddhair anyat pramāṇaṃ ca ko 'smin arthe jinādhikaḥ || RATNA_04.91
children.translated_text: [in the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s>] by the <s>Buddhas</s>; and what other authority on this matter surpasses the <s>Jina</s> (Conqueror)?

children.text: adhiṣṭānāryasatyārthabodhipakṣopasaṃhitāt |
children.translated_text: From the path common to the <s>Śrāvakas</s>, comprising the foundations, the meaning of the noble truths,

children.text: mārgāc chrāvakasāmānyād bauddhaṃ kenādhikaṃ phalaṃ || RATNA_04.92
children.translated_text: and the factors of awakening — how could the fruit of Buddhahood, which is superior, [be obtained]?

children.text: bodhicaryāpratiṣṭhārthaṃ na sūtre bhāṣitaṃ vacaḥ |
children.translated_text: Words for the establishment of the conduct toward awakening have not been spoken in the <s>sūtras</s> [of the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s>],

children.text: bhāṣitaṃ ca mahāyāne grāhyam asmād vicakṣaṇaiḥ || RATNA_04.93
children.translated_text: but they have been spoken in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>; therefore, this should be accepted by the discerning.

children.text: yathaiva vaiyākaraṇo mātṛkām api pāṭhayet |
children.translated_text: Just as a grammarian would teach even the alphabet,

children.text: buddho 'vadat tathā dharmaṃ vineyānāṃ yathākṣamaṃ || RATNA_04.94
children.translated_text: so the <s>Buddha</s> taught the <s>Dharma</s> to those to be trained according to their capacity.

children.text: keṣāṃcid avadad dharmaṃ pāpebhyo vinivṛttaye |
children.translated_text: To some he taught the <s>Dharma</s> for turning away from sins;

children.text: keṣāṃcit puṇyasiddhyarthaṃ keṣāṃcid dvayaniḥśritaṃ || RATNA_04.95
children.translated_text: to some, for the accomplishment of merit; to some, [a teaching] based on duality.

children.text: dvayāniśritam ekeṣāṃ gāmbhīraṃ bhīrubhīṣaṇaṃ |
children.translated_text: To some, [a teaching] not based on duality, profound, frightening to the fearful;

children.text: śūnyatākaruṇāgarbham ekeṣāṃ bodhisādhanaṃ || RATNA_04.96
children.translated_text: to some, the means of enlightenment, whose essence is <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) and <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion).

children.text: iti sadbhir mahāyāne kartavyaḥ pratighakṣayaḥ |
children.translated_text: Therefore, the wise should destroy hostility toward the <s>Mahāyāna</s>,

children.text: prasādaś cādhikaḥ kāryaḥ saṃyaksaṃbodhisiddhaye || RATNA_04.97
children.translated_text: and should cultivate increased faith, for the accomplishment of perfect complete awakening.

children.text: mahāyānaprasādena taduktācaraneṇa ca |
children.translated_text: Through devotion to the <s>Mahāyāna</s> (Great Vehicle) and through the practice taught therein,

children.text: prāpyate 'nuttarā bodhiḥ sarvasaukhyāni cāntarā || RATNA_04.98
children.translated_text: unsurpassed <s>bodhi</s> (awakening) is attained, and all happinesses in the interim. // RATNA 4.98

children.text: dānaśīlakṣamāsatyaṃ gṛhasthasya viśeṣataḥ |
children.translated_text: Generosity (<s>dāna</s>), moral conduct (<s>śīla</s>), forbearance (<s>kṣamā</s>), and truthfulness —

children.text: dharma uktaḥ kṛpāgarbhaḥ sa sātmīkriyatāṃ dṛḍhaṃ || RATNA_04.99
children.translated_text: this is the <s>Dharma</s> taught especially for the householder, whose essence is compassion (<s>kṛpā</s>); let it be firmly made one's own. // RATNA 4.99

children.text: atha lokasya vaidharmyād rājyaṃ dharmeṇa duṣkaraṃ |
children.translated_text: Now, because of the world's unrighteousness, rulership through <s>Dharma</s> is difficult;

children.text: tato dharmayaśo 'rthaṃ te prayujyādhigamaḥ kṣamaḥ || RATNA_04.100
children.translated_text: therefore, for the sake of your fame in <s>Dharma</s>, an attainment through [devoted] effort is fitting. // RATNA 4.100

children.text: ratnāvalyām rājavṛttopadeśe nāma caturthaḥ paricchedaḥ |
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fourth chapter, entitled 'Instruction on Royal Conduct,' in the <s>Ratnāvalī</s> (Precious Garland).
